style.summary:
style of A: A speaks plainly and matter-of-factly, relaying a suggestion and then refining it with 'I mean'.
style of B: B responds with short exclamations such as 'Hmm!' and 'Oh!' and a closing 'I see.'

A: A's plain, factual delivery makes A sound knowledgeable about the suggestion.
A's reference to a named expert lends A's claim authority.
A's refinement with 'I mean' shows A is clarifying a point that B has just heard.
B: B's short 'I see.' sounds conclusive and ends the exchange on B's terms.
B's exclamations show B reacting to A's content in a way that shapes how A continues.
B's brevity keeps B from committing to a position that A could challenge.

A: Plain delivery is not authority, and B's 'I see' suggests B is only acknowledging what A said.
Naming an expert is a claim that B can accept or doubt, so the authority is not A's alone.
Refining a point can be a sign of A backing off, which gives B the final assessment.
B: 'I see' is a closing acknowledgement, not a decision, so it does not decide the outcome.
Reactions that prompt A to continue are passive, and A still chooses what to say.
Brevity can also mean B has no position, which leaves A to define the suggestion.

content.summary:
content of A: A relays a suggestion from a named expert that the way to deal with noisy speech is to add noise to all the data.
content of B: B offers no substantive content and only reacts to the suggestion.

A: A supplies the entire substance of the exchange through the suggestion.
A's reference to a named expert gives the content a source and a claim to credibility.
A's refinement to moderate noise defines the actual method under discussion.
B: B's reactions show B has taken the suggestion in, which lets B form a view later.
B's silence on the specifics leaves the question of the method open for B to test.
B's 'I see' shows B has accepted the framing for now.

A: A supplies the content, but it is an idea B has yet to endorse, so the substance is not settled.
The source is an expert A cites, and B does not have to accept the attribution.
Refining the method is A's choice, and B could have shaped it further.
B: Taking the suggestion in is passive, and it gives B no substantive contribution to the exchange.
Leaving the question open means B has not shaped the content of the discussion.
Accepting the framing for now is a concession that favours A's content.

coordination.summary:
coordination of A: A holds the turns and adds a second part to the suggestion after B's reaction.
coordination of B: B takes very short reactive turns that prompt A to keep going.

A: A holds the floor through the suggestion and its refinement.
A continues after each of B's reactions, so A controls the progression.
A ends the exchange with the final content, so A has the last substantive word.
B: B's short reactions give A the signal to continue, which shows B managing the pace.
B's 'I see' closes the exchange, which shows B deciding when it ends.
B's reactions interrupt the flow at points that B selects.

A: Holding the floor is possible only because B allows it, so B effectively controls the length.
Continuing after each reaction is what a speaker does when the listener is quiet.
Having the last word on content does not mean A controls the timing of the closing.
B: Short reactions do not manage the pace, since A decides what to say next.
Closing with 'I see' is an acknowledgement, not a decision about how the exchange ends.
Reactions at points B chose are fairly minor interruptions that do not shape the turns.

engagement.summary:
engagement of A: A engages with a concrete idea and expands on it to make sure B understands.
engagement of B: B engages through reactions that show surprise and interest, but offers no questions or elaboration.

A: A expands the suggestion to make it clearer, which shows A's investment in the idea.
A's concrete method shows A is engaged with a practical problem.
A's clarification shows A cares whether B understands.
B: B's exclamations show B is responding to A's idea with interest.
B's reactions keep the exchange lively and encourage A to elaborate.
B's 'I see' shows B has taken the idea on board.

A: Expanding the idea is a response to B's reactions, so B's interest drives the expansion.
A concrete method is A's contribution, but it is not shown to be what B wants to discuss.
Clarifying can be a sign that A is uncertain of B's reaction, which weakens A's position.
B: Reactions are brief and do not show the depth of engagement that A's elaboration shows.
Encouraging A to talk is a passive form of engagement, so A is the one investing effort.
Taking an idea on board is the minimum of engagement and does not show B's own commitment.
